name: Two-pass volume rendering
definition: A two-pass rendering technique that separates light attenuation computation from color compositing. The first pass renders volume slices to accumulate light in a dedicated light buffer. The second pass (eye pass) composites slices front-to-back using the attenuated light from the light buffer, applying an 'under' blend to accumulate color and opacity.
summary: Two-pass volume rendering decouples light attenuation from color compositing by separating the workload into a light pass and an eye pass, differing from single-pass ray marching by allowing efficient reuse of precomputed light attenuation.
